ev.q: Compared with 2019, overall pediatric emergency department visits decreased by 51%, 22%, and 23% during 2020, 2021, and January 2022
with an increase of eight visits per week in 2020 (VR = 3.94)
Weekly number and proportion of ED visits increased for certain types of injuries
compared them with corresponding weeks in 2019
Among children aged 5–11 years, the number and proportion of cannabis-involved visits increased during 2020 and 2021 compared with 2019
CDC assessed data from the National Syndromic Surveillance Program
compared them with corresponding weeks in 2019

methods_quotes.q: analyses were restricted to facilities with a coefficient of variation ≤40 and average weekly informative discharge diagnosis ≥75% complete
categories were restricted to those with a total difference of ≥100 visits between surveillance and comparison periods.
VRs were calculated as the proportion of all ED visits in each diagnostic category during the pandemic surveillance period
VRs were suppressed if there were <100 visits, the difference in visit counts between periods was <100, or the relative standard error was >30%.
CIs that excluded 1 were considered statistically significant.
